verdict.rationale: Obsidian's core app runs entirely on the user's own device. It works offline, needs no sign-up, and stores notes as local plain Markdown, so the core product never depends on vendor infrastructure. Users can also bring their own sync via Git or other third-party services. However, its server-side features (Sync, Publish) are documented only as Obsidian-hosted cloud services, and nothing in the pack shows a self-hostable server or deployable source. Missing for 10: self-hostable Sync/Publish servers, documented self-hosting or deployment path, source availability, independent corroboration of self-hosted setups.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Obsidian uses non-proprietary plain text Markdown files stored locally on your device. You have total control over your data, which means you can use Obsidian offline
Free without limits. No sign-up required.
Obsidian syncs with Obsidian Sync, Dropbox, iCloud, OneDrive, Git, and many other third-party services.
Obsidian Publish is a cloud-based hosting service
